parsed.explanation: Worst documented features combine state threat-framing with state-tolerated targeting: an October 2025 presidential decree listing LGBTQ people among national-defence threats, tied to an August 2026 surge of vigilante mob attacks on trans women, alongside venue raids (75 arrested June 2025) and public caning under Aceh's Islamic code for a 'person with gender disorder'. A trans traveller died in police custody (2022) after an alleged US$100,000 extortion demand — a severity-5, state-implicated case. The 2026 penal code criminalises all extramarital (effectively same-sex) sex with up to 2 years, selectively enforced; the pornography law carries 7 years. Pathologisation, broadcasting/app bans, 94 documented abuse cases and no operative anti-discrimination remedy complete the picture. Subnational variation exists, but national police protection is not demonstrated and Aceh's religious enforcement is real. Below the 0.25 tier (which lacks official threat-framing plus a traveller death in custody), but short of a near-certain execution campaign.
